cases.rationale: ...Bb4 skewers the knight on c5 in front of the rook. Na4 or Ne6 saves the knight at the cost of ...Bxe7.
...c5 forks the rook and queen. The rook can retreat to d1 and then ...cxb4 wins the queen.
Rh1 catches the queen on h2. Qxh1 Rxh1 gives up the queen for a rook. Qc2+ also loses the queen despite the possible rook liquidation.
Bc1 attacks the queen on e3 and the bishop behind it on h6. Qe2 saves the queen and Bxh6 wins the bishop instead.
...Ba6 cuts off the queen on b5. Qxa6 is the least costly retreat, giving up the queen for the bishop and later rook with Bxa6.
...Bh6 catches the queen on f4. Qg5 loses the queen, Qxh6 allows the attack on a2, and Qe3 or Qd2 allows mate.
Ng4 forks rook and queen. ...Re6 saves the rook and Nxf6+ takes the queen instead.
Qc2 threatens mate on h7 and attacks the knight on b3. Every knight retreat allows immediate mate; a defence against mate loses the knight.
Ne4 leaves Black with multiple severe threats. Qd8 preserves the queen for the checked horizon while Qxf8+ wins the rook. Attribution of the full loss to a queen trap alone is unclear.
...Bf5 attacks the queen on e4 and restricts its exits. Rxd8 Bxe4 Rxf8+ limits the loss. Qd5 Rxd5 also loses the queen.
...Bc5 leaves the queen on a7 with no safe retreat. Qxc5 Qxc5 gives up the queen for a bishop.
...Na5 traps the queen on b7. Qxa8 Qxa8 or Qb4 Bxb4 axb4 are material concessions.
Ra2 catches the queen on b2. After ...Qxa2 Qxa2 the rook is the maximum immediate return.
Na4 catches the queen on b2; ...Qxa1 Qxa1 exchanges the queen for a rook, and ...Qe5 also loses the queen.
Na4 catches the queen on b2. ...Qxa3 Rxa3 Bxa3 and ...Qxa1 Qxa1 both concede the queen.
...Na5 catches the queen on c4. Moving to d5, a4 or b5 loses it. Pushing d4 or Nd5 leaves it on c4 to be captured.
...Nc5 catches the queen on b7. Qxa8 Qxa8 is the best salvage. After the prior bishop capture, the loss from the pre-mistake board is smaller than the cost of the retreat.
...Bg4 attacks and catches the queen on f3. Qxg4 Nxg4 and Qd1 Bxd1 lose it. d6 allows Bxf3 and counterplay with dxe7.
...Be5 catches the queen on g7. Qxh8+ Bxh8 is best salvage and also opens a later capture on a1.
Bc4 catches the queen on b3. ...Qxc4 Qxc4 trades the queen for a bishop. ...Bc5+ first is a checking intermezzo in the engine line.

limitations: One engine-assisted review. Paired root lines, unrestricted replies, and searches forcing each legal retreat of the attacked piece were checked before examining any classifier outputs.
A trap requires the attacked piece to have no viable retreat, including concessions caused by a mating threat. A viable escape with an unrelated piece loss is a different mechanism.
The capture-based retrieval filter intentionally overrepresents tactical errors. The reviewed trap negatives are other tactical mechanisms, and the positional axis was outside this reference scope.
